descriptions.description: A unit-conversion prompt asks for the speed of light, 3.0 x 10^8 meters per second, in kilometers per second using the kilo prefix 10^3.

A worked unit-conversion solution converts 3 x 10^8 meters per second to 3 x 10^5 kilometers per second, then uses 1 mile per 1.609 kilometers to obtain about 1.9 x 10^5 miles per second with significant-figure annotations.
The slide defines instantaneous velocity as the limit of average velocity as delta t approaches zero and shows the handwritten result vector v equals d vector x over dt.
The slide explains working backward from acceleration to velocity and from velocity to position by integration, emphasizing interpretation as area under the curve.
A handwritten substitution solves two kinematics equations for the runner acceleration, producing a_R equals 2 over t squared times the quantity x_g0 minus x_R0 plus v_g t.
The slide defines two-dimensional vector components and asks for the x and y components of a 24 meter vector at 65 degrees counterclockwise from the positive x axis.
